text: The Ministry of Health (Spanish: Ministerio de Salud) of Argentina is a ministry within the national executive power responsible for overseeing, formulating, and coordinating the country's public health policy. It manages Argentina's highly decentralized universal health care system, which, according to 2000 data, served over half of the population. Since 30 September 2024, Mario Lugones has served as Minister of Health, appointed by President Javier Milei. The Ministry of Health and Sustainable Development includes centralized dependencies such as secretariats, undersecretariats, and other centralized agencies, each comprising directorates and agencies that assess various healthcare areas. Several deconcentrated agencies report to the ministry, including the Superintendency of Health Services (SSS), the National Agency of Public Laboratories (ANLAP), the Comprehensive Medical Attention Program (PAMI), the National Administration of Medicine, Food and Medical Technology (ANMAT), the Dr. Carlos Malbrán National Administration of Laboratories and Healthcare Institutes (ANLIS Malbrán), and the National Cancer and National Tropical Medicine Institutes. Additionally, decentralized agencies such as the National Psycho-physical Rehabilitation Institute of the South (INAREPS), the Only Central National Institute for Excision and Implants (Incucai), the Dr. Manuel Montes de Oca National Summer Camp, and the Baldomero Sommer, Laura Bonaparte and Alejandro Posadas national hospitals report to the ministry. The Ministry has been headquartered in the Ministry of Public Works Building since 1991, a structure originally serving as the headquarters of the Ministry of Public Works. This building is now an iconic landmark in Buenos Aires, located at the intersection of 9 de Julio Avenue and Belgrano Avenue in the Monserrat neighborhood, known for its large framed steel images of Eva Perón on the southern and northern facades.
